- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to compensate for bearish bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+3% from prior day), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast peak at +2% above prior high or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (≥0.75) and model forecast is flat or declining, force a slight upward bias (e.g., +0.3–0.8% per day) to align with sentiment.
- Mean reversion is common in 7–14 day horizons; if forecast is >+1.5% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 0.2–0.5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >1.5% from 18-day average, apply a “sentiment-weighted correction”: if sentiment >0.5, add 0.3% to forecast; if <0.3, subtract 0.3%.
